title: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027: Fully Funded PhD Scholarship in Canada for International and Canadian Students
summary: The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027 is now accepting applications from exceptional doctoral students whose research falls broadly within the humanities and social sciences and addresses important issues relevant to Canada and the wider world. The prestigious doctoral scholarship provides substantial financial support, research and travel funding, mentorship, experiential learning opportunities, and access to a multidisciplinary community of Scholars, Fellows, Mentors, and alumni. For the 2027 competition, applicants must first complete an eligibility verification process before they can access the full scholarship application. The deadline to request eligibility confirmation is October 2, 2026 , while the final application deadline is November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET . Opportunity Overview Opportunity: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship 2027 Category: Scholarship Study level: PhD/Doctoral Fields: Humanities and Social Sciences Study location: Canada, with specific eligibility provisions for Canadian students studying abroad Scholarship duration: Three years Annual stipend: Up to $50,000 Research, networking and travel allowance: Up to $20,000 per year Eligibility verification deadline: October 2, 2026 Reference deadline: October 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. ET Complete application deadline: November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET Application process: Two steps Official organization: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation About the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship is designed to support outstanding doctoral researchers whose work can contribute to important conversations and challenges affecting Canada and society. The Foundation is not simply looking for students with excellent grades. Its selection approach considers the broader potential of applicants, including their intellectual curiosity, leadership potential, engagement with society, ability to communicate knowledge, and capacity to create meaningful impact beyond academia. Successful Scholars become part of a multidisciplinary community where academic research is connected with public dialogue, mentorship, experiential learning, networking, and societal engagement. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant for doctoral students who want their research to have an influence beyond academic publications and contribute to wider discussions about major social, environmental, political, cultural, and human challenges. Scholarship Benefits One of the major attractions of the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship is its combination of financial support and professional development. 1. Annual stipend of up to $50,000 Selected Scholars can receive up to $50,000 per year for three years to support tuition and living expenses associated with their doctoral studies. Over the three-year scholarship period, this represents potential stipend support of up to $150,000 . The funding is intended to give doctoral researchers greater financial stability while they concentrate on their studies and research. 2. Research, networking and travel allowance Scholars can also receive up to $20,000 per year for three years to support activities connected to their doctoral work. This allowance can help support: Research-related activities Academic and professional travel Networking Participation in relevant events Activities connected with Foundation programming Other research-related opportunities This additional funding can be particularly valuable for researchers whose projects require fieldwork, conferences, collaboration, or engagement beyond their home institution. 3. Mentorship and experiential learning The scholarship goes beyond financial assistance by providing Scholars with opportunities to engage with Mentors and Fellows. The Foundation s programming can include: Meetings Masterclasses Seminars Conferences Leadership development Experiential learning Interdisciplinary exchanges Public policy discussions These opportunities are designed to broaden Scholars perspectives and help them connect their academic research with practical societal challenges. 4. Multidisciplinary community Successful applicants become part of a community involving Scholars, Fellows and Mentors working across different disciplines and sectors. This community can provide opportunities to: Exchange ideas across academic disciplines Develop professional relationships Learn from experienced researchers and leaders Share research with broader audiences Explore interdisciplinary approaches Participate in conversations about major societal issues 5. Alumni network Scholars also become part of the Foundation s alumni network, which includes more than 500 alumni . This creates a long-term professional and intellectual network that can continue beyond the three-year scholarship period. Fields of Study and Research Themes Applicants must be pursuing doctoral research broadly related to the humanities or social sciences . However, being in one of these broad academic fields is not enough. The proposed PhD research must also address issues relevant to Canada s future and align with at least one of the Foundation s four foundational themes . The four themes are: 1. Human Rights and Dignity This theme focuses on issues surrounding human rights, dignity, equality, justice, inclusion, and the conditions necessary for individuals and communities to live with dignity. Potential research areas may include questions related to: Human rights Social justice Equality Inclusion Discrimination Rights and freedoms Vulnerable populations Human dignity 2. Responsible Citizenship This theme concerns citizenship, participation, democratic life, civic engagement, and the responsibilities individuals and institutions have within society. Research connected to this theme may explore: Democracy Civic participation Citizenship Governance Political engagement Social responsibility Community participation Public institutions 3. Canada and the World This theme examines Canada s relationship with the international community and Canada s role in global affairs. Relevant research could address: International relations Globalization Diplomacy Migration International development Global governance Canada s international role Cross-border social and political issues 4. People and Their Natural Environment This theme explores relationships between people, society and the natural environment. Potential research areas may include: Environmental policy Climate change Sustainability Environmental justice Human-environment relationships Natural resource governance Ecological challenges Sustainable development Applicants should therefore ensure that their research proposal clearly demonstrates how their doctoral project connects with at least one of these four themes. Who Can Apply for the 2027 Scholarship? The Foundation has established specific citizenship and enrollment requirements. Eligible applicants must fall into one of three categories : Canadian students enrolled at a Canadian university Canadian students enrolled at a university outside Canada International students enrolled at a Canadian university This means international students can apply, but they must be enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university . Importantly, international students who are residing outside Canada and enrolled at a university outside Canada are not eligible for this particular scholarship. Therefore, applicants should carefully distinguish between citizenship and university enrollment when determining eligibility. PhD Stage Requirements The 2027 scholarship is specifically targeted at early-stage doctoral researchers. At the time of application, candidates must be either: In the first year of their PhD program , or In the second year of their PhD program . Applicants who are beyond the second year of their doctoral program should therefore carefully assess whether they meet the Foundation s requirements before beginning the application. There is no age limit for applying to the scholarship. What Does the Foundation Look For? Academic excellence is important, but the Foundation evaluates applicants more broadly. The strongest candidates are expected to demonstrate several qualities. Academic Excellence Applicants should have an outstanding academic record and demonstrate strong intellectual ability. Academic performance is assessed across the application, including: Academic transcripts Research proposal Letters of recommendation Overall application quality The Foundation states that successful applicants stand out through the quality of their research and their academic excellence. Intellectual Curiosity The Foundation seeks doctoral researchers who demonstrate genuine curiosity and an ambition to explore important questions. Your application should therefore demonstrate not only what you are researching, but also: Why the question matters What makes the research intellectually significant What knowledge gap you are addressing What new perspectives your work could contribute Leadership Potential Applicants should demonstrate potential to contribute positively beyond their immediate academic environment. Leadership does not necessarily have to mean holding a formal leadership position. It can be demonstrated through: Community initiatives Research collaborations Advocacy Professional activities Student leadership Public engagement Projects that have produced meaningful results Commitment to Society The Foundation places considerable emphasis on applicants who are interested in connecting research with society. Strong applications should show how the applicant s work could contribute to broader conversations or help address significant societal challenges. Potential for Impact Beyond Academia Applicants should think carefully about how their research can reach audiences outside universities. This could involve: Public policy Communities Civil society Government Professional organizations Practitioners Public education Knowledge translation The Foundation specifically emphasizes the importance of sharing knowledge and creating meaningful impact beyond academia. Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing The Foundation also values applicants who are willing to engage in dialogue, interdisciplinary collaboration, and knowledge exchange. A strong candidate should therefore be able to demonstrate an openness to learning from people working in other disciplines and sectors. Letters of Reference Applicants must provide three letters of reference . The three referees must include: One PhD supervisor One additional academic referee One referee from outside academia The inclusion of a non-academic referee is particularly important because the Foundation is interested in applicants broader engagement and potential impact beyond academia. Applicants should therefore select referees strategically rather than simply choosing individuals based on academic seniority. A good referee should ideally be able to provide specific evidence of your: Academic ability Research potential Leadership Community or professional engagement Communication skills Commitment to societal impact Potential for future contribution How the 2027 Application Process Works The 2027 competition introduces a two-step application process . Step 1: Eligibility Verification Applicants must first complete a short eligibility verification form. This initial step allows the Foundation to confirm whether an applicant meets the scholarship s eligibility requirements. The eligibility verification request must be submitted by: October 2, 2026. Applicants should not wait until the final day if they can avoid it. Reviewing the eligibility requirements in advance can help identify potential problems before submission. Step 2: Full Scholarship Application Only applicants whose eligibility has been confirmed will receive access to the full application form. This means applicants cannot simply skip the eligibility verification stage and proceed directly to the full application . The Foundation states that applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed. Important 2027 Scholarship Deadlines Applicants should keep track of all dates rather than focusing only on the final application deadline. September 1, 2026 The 2027 application process opens, including the eligibility verification form. October 2, 2026 Deadline to submit an eligibility confirmation request. This is the first major deadline and should not be confused with the final application deadline. Weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026 Mandatory information sessions. Eligible applicants should pay attention to instructions from the Foundation regarding participation in these sessions. October 30, 2026 — 9:00 a.m. ET Deadline for all three reference letters to be received. Applicants should contact referees well in advance because the letters must be received by the deadline. November 6, 2026 — 4:00 p.m. ET Final deadline for submitting the complete scholarship application. How to Prepare a Strong Application Because the scholarship is highly selective, applicants should approach the application strategically. 1. Confirm Your Eligibility Early Before investing significant time in the application, check: Your citizenship status Your university s location Your current PhD year Your field of study Your research topic Your alignment with the four Foundation themes This is especially important for international applicants because international students must be enrolled at a Canadian university. 2. Develop a Clear Research Narrative Your research proposal should make it easy for reviewers to understand: The problem you are investigating Why the problem matters The research gap Your research questions Your approach The expected contribution The relevance of your work to Canada and society How your research connects to the Foundation s themes Avoid presenting your project as merely an academic exercise. Explain why the research matters in the real world. 3. Clearly Connect Your Research to a Foundation Theme Do not assume reviewers will automatically see the connection. Explicitly explain how your research relates to one or more of: Human Rights and Dignity Responsible Citizenship Canada and the World People and their Natural Environment A well-developed thematic connection can help demonstrate that your project fits the Foundation s objectives. 4. Demonstrate Impact Think beyond publications and academic conferences. Explain how your research could potentially influence: Public policy Communities Institutions Professional practice Public understanding Social debates Government decision-making 5. Choose Your Referees Carefully Because three references are required and one must come from outside academia, applicants should begin approaching potential referees early. Give referees sufficient information about: Your research The scholarship Your achievements Your goals The Foundation s themes Why you believe you are a strong candidate This makes it easier for referees to write detailed and relevant recommendations. 6. Demonstrate Engagement Beyond Academia If you have participated in community projects, professional initiatives, policy discussions, advocacy, public communication, volunteering, or other activities related to your research, explain their relevance. The Foundation is interested in researchers who can connect knowledge with society. APPLY HERE Why This Scholarship Is Different from a Conventional PhD Scholarship Many doctoral scholarships primarily focus on financial support. The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship combines financial assistance with an extensive intellectual and professional development component. The Foundation describes its scholarship as more than financial support, emphasizing mentorship, experiential learning, community engagement and knowledge sharing. A Scholar therefore gains access to: Substantial doctoral funding Research and travel support Mentorship Leadership opportunities Interdisciplinary discussions Experiential learning Professional networking A multidisciplinary community A long-term alumni network For doctoral students interested in connecting academic research with real-world challenges, this broader model can be particularly valuable. Frequently Asked Questions Can international students apply? Yes. International students are eligible if they are enrolled in a doctoral program at a Canadian university . International students residing outside Canada and enrolled at universities outside Canada are not eligible. Can Canadian students studying outside Canada apply? Yes. Canadian students enrolled at universities outside Canada can apply, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements. Can students in their third year of a PhD apply? No. For the 2027 competition, applicants must be in their first or second year of doctoral studies at the time of application . Is there an age limit? No. The Foundation states that there is no age limit for applicants. Do applicants have to speak both English and French? No. Applicants do not need to be fluent in both official languages. However, they must be able to communicate effectively in either English or French . How much is the scholarship worth? The scholarship provides up to $50,000 per year for three years , plus up to $20,000 per year for research, networking and travel . Is the scholarship renewable? The scholarship is structured as a three-year program . Can Scholars receive other scholarships? Yes, but the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship may be adjusted depending on funding received from other organizations, universities or institutions. Scholars must declare additional sources of income each year. The Foundation states that, regardless of other funding, Scholars continue to receive the annual research allowance, while the annual stipend has a minimum level of $25,000. Application Link Applicants should begin by reviewing the official eligibility requirements and then completing the eligibility verification process. Applicants with questions about the 2027 scholarship can contact the Foundation at scholarship2027@trudeaufoundation.ca . Visit HERE to learn more about the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027. Conclusion The Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation Scholarship 2027 is a major opportunity for early-stage doctoral researchers in the humanities and social sciences who want to combine academic excellence with leadership, public engagement and meaningful societal impact. The scholarship offers up to $50,000 annually for three years , an additional $20,000 per year for research, networking and travel , mentorship, experiential learning, interdisciplinary engagement and access to a community of more than 500 alumni. However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The opportunity is open to Canadian students studying in Canada or abroad, as well as international students enrolled at Canadian universities. Applicants must also be in the first or second year of their PhD and their research must fall broadly within the humanities or social sciences while aligning with at least one of the Foundation s four themes. The first critical deadline is October 2, 2026 , when applicants must submit their eligibility confirmation request. Those who pass the eligibility stage must then ensure their three references are received by October 30, 2026 , and submit the complete application by November 6, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. ET . For prospective Scholars, the key to a competitive application is not simply demonstrating strong academic performance. Applicants should present a compelling research project, clearly articulate its relevance to Canada and society, demonstrate leadership and engagement, and show how their work can create impact beyond academia. title: Brooke Owens Fellowship 2027: Applications Open for Undergraduate Students Seeking Careers in Aerospace
summary: Brooke Owens Fellowship 2027: Applications Open for Undergraduate Students Seeking Careers in Aerospace Applications are officially open for the Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027 , an internationally accessible program designed to help talented undergraduate women and gender-minority students launch and accelerate careers across the aerospace and aviation industries. The 2027 application cycle opened on September 1, 2026 , and applications must be submitted by October 4, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) . The official application portal describes the program as bringing together exceptional undergraduate students from around the world who are passionate about aerospace careers and want to become future leaders in the industry. The program goes beyond traditional academic assessment. Applicants are evaluated as complete individuals, with attention given to their experiences, interests, aspirations, creativity, character, service, leadership potential and the contribution they could make to the wider aerospace community. Official Brooke Owens Fellowship 2027 Application Information Brooke Owens Fellowship 2027 at a Glance Detail Information Program Brooke Owens Fellowship Class of 2027 Application opening September 1, 2026 Application deadline October 4, 2026 Deadline time 11:59 PM EDT Target applicants Undergraduate women and gender-minority students Age requirement At least 18 years old Academic level Undergraduate Required coursework At least one year toward an associate or bachelor s degree Academic major Any major is welcome Career interest Aerospace industry Nationality All nationalities may apply U.S. citizenship Not required Main experience Summer aerospace industry experience/internship Mentorship One-on-one professional/executive mentorship Professional development Included Summit Brooke Owens professional development summit Application platform Online Recommendation One letter required Personal statement Maximum 600 words Mission Alignment Essay Maximum 300 words Multimedia submission Under 250 MB and reviewable in no more than five minutes Minimum GPA None stated The application portal opened at 12:00 AM EDT on September 1, 2026 and closes at 11:59 PM EDT on October 4, 2026 . What Is the Brooke Owens Fellowship? The Brooke Owens Fellowship was created to expand opportunities for undergraduate women and gender minorities who want to become leaders, innovators and contributors within aerospace. The program is named in honor of Dawn Brooke Owens , an accomplished aerospace professional and pilot whose career included work connected with NASA s Johnson Space Center, the XPRIZE Foundation, the Federal Aviation Administration s Office of Commercial Space Transportation and the White House Office of Management and Budget. The initiative was founded by aerospace leaders who knew Brooke personally and wanted to create opportunities for a new generation of people who could bring similar talent, creativity, determination and commitment to service into the industry. Today, the program focuses on providing career opportunities, mentorship, professional development, industry connections and a strong community for undergraduate women and gender-minority students interested in aerospace. The organization is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit and has developed a substantial network of aerospace professionals, executives, mentors, host organizations and alumni. Applications for the Class of 2027 Are Now Open The Class of 2027 represents the 11th group of Brooke Owens Fellows , marking more than a decade since the program s first fellowship class. Applications opened on September 1 and will remain open until October 4, 2026. The latest official announcement confirms that the opportunity is available to women and gender-minority undergraduate students from all college majors who are interested in careers in aerospace and aviation. This broad academic approach is important because aerospace is much larger than aerospace engineering alone. Professionals working in the sector may come from backgrounds including: Aerospace engineering Mechanical engineering Electrical engineering Computer science Artificial intelligence Data science Physics Mathematics Chemistry Biology Earth and environmental sciences Business Finance Communications Public relations Art and design Law Public policy International affairs Government Education STEM outreach The program s FAQ explicitly states that applicants do not have to major in aerospace engineering . Students from engineering, science, business, communications, art, law, policy and other academic fields may apply if they are seriously interested in building a career in aerospace. What Will Selected Brooke Owens Fellows Receive? The Brooke Owens Fellowship combines industry exposure with mentorship, community and professional development. For the Class of 2027, the official announcement states that successful Fellows will: Participate in a summer internship with a host company. Receive one-on-one mentorship from professionals aligned with their areas of interest. Attend a professional development summit with the other Fellows in their class. The Brooke Owens Fellowship also describes its broader program as providing access to paid internships and executive-level mentorship from senior aerospace figures, including executives, astronauts and industry leaders. Summer Aerospace Industry Experience A major element of the program is meaningful exposure to the aerospace industry. The 2027 program announcement states that accepted Fellows will participate in a summer internship at a host company . This provides students with the opportunity to move from classroom learning into professional aerospace environments and develop practical experience in the sector. Past Fellows have worked across areas such as: Rocket propulsion Satellite operations Mission planning Aerospace policy STEM outreach Engineering Software Space systems Research Communications Other aerospace-related functions. The fellowship is therefore relevant not only to students pursuing highly technical engineering careers but also to those interested in the business, policy, communications and social dimensions of aerospace. One-on-One Professional Mentorship Mentorship is another central feature of the Brooke Owens Fellowship. Each Fellow is connected with experienced professionals who can provide guidance as the Fellow enters or develops within the aerospace sector. The Fellowship s current mentor structure pairs Fellows with hand-selected mentors, with relationships beginning before Fellows start their summer positions. Mentors support Fellows as they prepare for professional roles, navigate workplace challenges and make decisions about their longer-term careers. Many mentor relationships reportedly continue beyond the official summer program. The program s mentors have included senior aerospace professionals, astronauts, executives, engineers and other industry leaders. For a university student preparing to enter a highly specialized sector, this kind of direct professional access can help with: Career planning. Understanding aerospace industry pathways. Developing professional networks. Navigating early-career decisions. Preparing for internships and employment. Learning directly from experienced aerospace leaders. Building professional confidence. Identifying future areas of specialization. Brooke Owens Professional Development Summit Selected Fellows also participate in the annual Brooke Owens Summit , which brings members of the fellowship class together for professional development. The 2027 announcement confirms that successful Fellows will attend a professional development summit alongside their cohort. The summit adds an important cohort component to the program. Rather than completing an internship independently, Fellows become part of a community of students pursuing careers across different parts of aerospace. This can create valuable relationships that continue as participants move into graduate education, industry, government, entrepreneurship, research and other aerospace careers. A Long-Term Aerospace Community The Fellowship is designed to create more than a one-summer experience. The official Class of 2027 application describes Fellows as joining a lasting community of: Peers. Mentors. Aerospace professionals. Industry leaders. This community-based model can be particularly valuable in aerospace, where professional relationships, specialized knowledge and industry networks can play an important role in career development. The goal stated by the program is not simply to help students obtain their first aerospace opportunity, but to help develop people who may eventually shape the future direction of the industry. More Than 400 Fellows Have Joined the Program The Brooke Owens Fellowship has grown significantly since its creation. According to the program s September 2026 announcement: 418 undergraduate students have been accepted since the program began. Fellows have come from nearly 40 U.S. states and territories . Participants have represented 10 countries . 124 companies have hosted Fellows for summer internships. 105 mentors have helped support Fellows during their early careers. Fellows have represented 147 schools . These figures demonstrate that the fellowship has developed into an established pathway connecting undergraduate talent with the aerospace industry. Detailed Eligibility Requirements Before beginning an application, candidates should carefully confirm that they satisfy every current requirement. The official Class of 2027 application page lists four principal eligibility conditions. 1. You Must Be an Undergraduate Student Applicants must currently be undergraduate students. They must have completed at least one year of coursework toward a bachelor s or associate degree by the time they apply. This means the program is aimed at students who have progressed beyond the very beginning of their undergraduate education. 2. You Must Be Interested in an Aerospace Career Applicants must demonstrate genuine interest in pursuing a career in the aerospace industry. Engineering and non-engineering career pathways are both accepted. Candidates therefore should not assume that admission is restricted to: Aerospace engineers. Mechanical engineers. Scientists. Technical majors. Students from other disciplines are encouraged to apply when they can demonstrate a credible connection between their interests and an aerospace career. 3. Applicants Must Identify as a Woman or Gender Minority The Fellowship is specifically designed to increase opportunities for people underrepresented in aerospace because of gender. The formal Class of 2027 eligibility criteria require applicants to identify as a woman or gender minority . The organization s FAQ specifically notes that this includes women and other gender minorities, including nonbinary and gender-nonconforming individuals. 4. Applicants Must Be at Least 18 Applicants must be 18 years of age or older . Students From All Academic Majors Can Apply One of the strongest features of the Brooke Owens Fellowship is that it recognizes the multidisciplinary nature of aerospace. Students do not have to study aerospace engineering. The official FAQ specifically welcomes applicants from academic backgrounds such as engineering, science, business, communications, art, law and policy, along with other disciplines. The critical factor is whether the applicant has a genuine ambition to build a career and create an impact within aerospace. Is There a Minimum GPA? No minimum GPA is stated. The Fellowship deliberately uses a broader approach to identifying talent. The official application guidance notes that past Fellows have included students with very high GPAs as well as students whose academic records were considerably lower. The organization states that GPA represents only one imperfect way of assessing an applicant s abilities and potential. The FAQ similarly states that applications are reviewed holistically, with consideration given to factors including the applicant s: Personal statement. Creative submission. Recommendation. Character. Leadership. Creativity. Service. Alignment with Fellowship values. Students should therefore not automatically rule themselves out because they do not have a perfect academic record. Documents You Need to Prepare The application requires several supporting materials. Applicants should start preparing these well before the October deadline because the process includes both conventional application documents and original creative work. Updated Resume or CV Applicants need their most recent resume or CV. The Fellowship recommends making sure the document is accurate, polished and carefully proofread. Relevant experience may include: Academic activities. Internships. Paid employment. Volunteer activities. Independent projects. Leadership positions. Clubs. Extracurricular activities. Relevant community involvement. Applicants should use the resume to show not merely academic performance but evidence that they could contribute effectively as a teammate and member of the aerospace community. Academic Transcript Applicants must submit their latest transcript. Importantly, an unofficial transcript is acceptable , and the Fellowship actually encourages students to use unofficial versions when obtaining an official transcript would require paying a fee. The transcript submitted must contain completed, graded coursework. The application guidance says it needs to include at least one full semester of completed grades , rather than only midterm results. Applicants studying at a new institution who do not yet have an appropriate transcript there may use a transcript from their previous institution where applicable. Note that the formal Class of 2027 eligibility section separately states that an applicant must have completed at least one year of coursework toward an associate or bachelor s degree . Applicants should therefore ensure they satisfy the formal eligibility requirement, rather than interpreting the transcript-upload requirement as reducing it to one semester. One Letter of Recommendation Only one recommendation letter is required. The recommender should be someone who genuinely knows the applicant and can provide meaningful evidence about their strengths, achievements and character. Potential recommenders may include: Teachers. Professors. Coaches. Mentors. Supervisors. Club leaders. Other appropriate professional or academic contacts. A family member or personal friend should not be used as the recommender. The letter should ideally provide evidence of the applicant s character, creativity, consistency, service and impact in the communities in which they participate. The official FAQ confirms that applicants need one recommendation and only one will be accepted . Three Original Application Components For 2027, applicants are asked to prepare three original works intended to help reviewers understand them beyond their transcript and resume. These are: A Personal Statement of no more than 600 words. A Mission Alignment Essay of no more than 300 words. A Multimedia Essay in a format other than a conventional written essay. Together, these submissions are intended to provide insight into three broad dimensions: Professional and academic interests. Personal character, values and passions. Commitment to service, community and creating opportunities for others. Personal Statement: Maximum 600 Words The personal statement allows applicants to communicate who they are beyond their academic record. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the passions, values, experiences, goals and personal qualities that have shaped them and their ambitions. The objective is not simply to repeat a resume. A strong personal statement should help reviewers understand: What motivates you. What experiences have shaped you. What matters to you. What kind of person you are. Where you want your career to go. What you would contribute to the Brooke Owens community. The program specifically encourages applicants to be authentic, specific and reflective. Mission Alignment Essay: Maximum 300 Words The 2027 application also includes a Mission Alignment Essay , limited to 300 words. This component asks candidates to reflect on the Brooke Owens Fellowship s mission of expanding aerospace opportunities for women and gender minorities. Applicants should explain why this mission matters to them and how they hope to contribute to it throughout their careers. Potential themes include: Creating more inclusive professional environments. Mentoring future students. Expanding access to aerospace opportunities. Addressing structural barriers. Using leadership positions to support others. Helping future professionals enter and thrive in aerospace. The Fellowship encourages applicants to connect their answers with their lived experiences and consider how they could use future leadership or influence to make aerospace more welcoming and equitable. Multimedia Essay: Show Creativity Beyond a Written Application The Multimedia Essay is deliberately different from a conventional university application essay. Applicants must not submit another traditional written essay. Instead, they should communicate their ideas through a creative digital format. Past formats have included: Short videos. Original songs. Spoken-word pieces. Animations. Graphic designs. Podcasts. Comic strips. Other creative digital formats. Multimedia Submission Requirements The submission must: Be fully digital. Require no physical mailing. Be accessible through commonly available software. Not require passwords or obscure software. Be reviewable or playable in five minutes or less. Remain below 250 MB in file size. 2027 Multimedia Essay Prompts Applicants can respond creatively to one of the prompts listed for the Class of 2027. The themes focus on: A situation where the applicant had to be resourceful and work within constraints. An experience serving a community and the resulting impact. A project or activity in which the applicant became deeply engaged and demonstrated enthusiasm or creativity. A situation where the applicant challenged an established system, norm or assumption. How intentional decision-making has influenced the applicant s actions and outcomes. These prompts are designed to reveal qualities such as: Resourcefulness. Creativity. Values. Service. Teamwork. Enthusiasm. Courage. Independent thinking. Leadership. Self-awareness. Intentionality. Important File Submission Rules Applicants should carefully test every file before submitting the application. The Fellowship specifically warns that an application cannot be edited after submission . Before submitting: Test video links. Confirm that file-sharing permissions work. Make sure reviewers will not encounter access restrictions. Check that all files open correctly. Verify multimedia runtime. Keep files below the required 250 MB limit. Proofread written documents. Confirm that the correct versions have been uploaded. The application page also recommends including the relevant prompt directly with each original work so reviewers can easily identify the question being addressed. One detail worth noting is that the current page explicitly identifies three original works , including the 300-word Mission Alignment Essay, while its later file-submission checklist lists the resume, transcript, recommendation letter, personal statement and multimedia essay without repeating the mission essay. Applicants should follow the live application portal carefully and prepare the Mission Alignment Essay because it is expressly listed as a required original work earlier on the official 2027 application page. Are International Students Eligible? Yes. U.S. citizenship is not required. The official FAQ states that students of all nationalities are welcome to apply , while the official application portal describes the fellowship as bringing together undergraduate students from around the world. There is, however, an important practical qualification for international applicants. Some aerospace opportunities may be subject to U.S. export-control or International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) restrictions. These requirements can limit eligibility for particular jobs or host-company roles based on citizenship or immigration status. The Fellowship states that it works with Fellows individually to identify opportunities that fit their circumstances. International students should therefore not interpret ITAR restrictions as a general ban on applying . They are eligible for the Fellowship itself, although the range of specific industry placements available to them may differ. Virtual Information Sessions for the Class of 2027 The Fellowship is also hosting virtual information sessions for prospective applicants. The published Class of 2027 sessions, with times given in EDT, are: September 13, 2026 at 2:00 PM EDT September 19, 2026 at 12:00 PM EDT , featuring international students September 28, 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT The session specifically featuring international students may be particularly useful for applicants with questions about citizenship requirements, aerospace placements and participation from outside the United States. Ask a Brookie Application Support Applicants who want advice from someone who has previously completed the fellowship process can use the program s Ask a Brookie resource. Past Fellows can provide guidance about matters such as: Their fellowship experience. How they approached application essays. Internship preparation. Joining the Fellowship community. General application strategy. For formal questions concerning eligibility, applicants are advised to use the Fellowship s official eligibility information or contact its administration rather than relying solely on peer advice. How Applicants Are Selected The program emphasizes holistic assessment rather than relying on one numerical indicator. According to its FAQ, applications are reviewed by aerospace professionals and Brooke Owens alumni. The program considers the overall application, including personal and creative materials, recommendations and alignment with the Fellowship s values. There is no published minimum GPA cutoff and no single factor automatically determines selection. This makes it important for applicants to submit a coherent application where the different components reinforce one another. For example: Your resume shows what you have done. Your transcript gives academic context. Your recommendation provides an outside perspective. Your personal statement shows who you are. Your Mission Alignment Essay explains how your values connect with the program. Your multimedia project demonstrates creativity, character and perspective. What Makes a Strong Application? While there is no guaranteed formula, applicants should pay particular attention to the qualities the Fellowship repeatedly emphasizes. Be Authentic Do not attempt to construct what you imagine a stereotypical aerospace candidate should look like. The application is specifically designed to identify talent that may not always be recognized through conventional recruitment methods. Demonstrate Service Community involvement is an important theme throughout the application. Show what you have actually done for other people, organizations or communities. Demonstrate Aerospace Interest You do not need to study aerospace engineering, but your application should make it credible that aerospace is genuinely part of your intended career direction. Show Creativity This matters particularly in the multimedia submission. Use a format that strengthens your message rather than selecting something elaborate simply because it appears impressive. Explain Your Values The program wants to understand what motivates your decisions and how your values affect the way you work with others. Proofread Everything A creative application can still be weakened by avoidable mistakes, inaccessible links or unclear writing. Start Early The application includes several components requiring substantial reflection, plus a recommendation from another person. Waiting until the final day substantially increases the risk of an incomplete or technically flawed application. title: 2030STEM Fellowship 2026: Apply for a US$10,000 Career Development Award for STEM Researchers and Professionals
summary: Applications are open for the 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 , a career-development opportunity designed to support early- to mid-career researchers and professionals working across science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and related STEM fields. For the 2026 cycle, 2030STEM is seeking five STEM professionals to serve as Fellows , with each selected Fellow receiving a US$10,000 award that can be used to advance their professional career. The fellowship is intended to provide flexible career-development support while recognizing STEM professionals who demonstrate leadership, community building, knowledge translation, and the potential to contribute to meaningful change within the STEM ecosystem. The funding can support a range of professional-development needs, including conference participation, research-related expenses, childcare, and other costs connected with career advancement. Rather than prescribing one single route to professional development, the program acknowledges that STEM professionals may face different financial, institutional, professional, and personal barriers at different stages of their careers. 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity 2030STEM Fellowship Application 2026 Organizer 2030STEM Number of Fellows 5 Award US$10,000 per selected Fellow Target Group Early- to mid-career STEM researchers and professionals Fields STEM disciplines and professional areas Funding Purpose Career development Examples of Eligible Uses Conference travel, research expenses, childcare and other career-development needs Application Method Online application References Required Names and email addresses of three references CV/Resume Required Selection Emphasis Community building, knowledge translation and innovative STEM leadership Application Deadline Not stated on the current 2026 application form Application Status The online application form was live when reviewed on September 4, 2026 The current application form does not display a formal closing date. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that applications will remain open indefinitely and should consider submitting as early as possible after confirming that they meet the intended applicant profile. What Is the 2030STEM Fellowship? 2030STEM describes the initiative as a catalytic resource intended to advance the careers of STEM researchers and professionals. The central idea behind the fellowship is that scientific and technological progress depends not only on institutions, laboratories and funding mechanisms but also on the people conducting research, communicating scientific knowledge, building professional communities and providing leadership. The program therefore seeks professionals who can advance their own careers while also contributing to improvements in the broader culture and structure of STEM. According to the 2026 application, successful candidates are expected to have demonstrated a strong history in three important areas: Building community. Translating knowledge. Demonstrating innovative leadership in STEM. These elements indicate that applicants should present themselves not simply as technically qualified scientists or professionals but as individuals whose work has influenced colleagues, communities, institutions, research environments or wider audiences. About 2030STEM 2030STEM is an initiative working toward systemic change within science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Its broader work focuses on areas including: Full inclusion in STEM. Leadership development. Institutional change. Access to capital. Professional advancement. Community development. Improved pathways for historically underrepresented STEM professionals. 2030STEM states that its work takes a systems-level approach to strengthening professional self-efficacy, STEM and cultural identities, self-advocacy, leadership pathways and institutional structures. The organization particularly emphasizes increasing representation and leadership opportunities for Black, Latino/a/x, Indigenous and other people of color throughout STEM disciplines and sectors. Its broader strategy includes improving access to professional networks, capital, leadership opportunities and institutional support. Why the 2030STEM Fellowship Matters Career advancement in STEM can require resources that traditional research grants, university funding or employer budgets do not always cover. Researchers and professionals may need financial support to: Attend important scientific conferences. Conduct or advance research. Access professional-development opportunities. Build collaborations. Travel to laboratories, institutions or meetings. Obtain equipment or other resources connected with professional advancement. Manage childcare responsibilities while participating in professional activities. Strengthen their professional networks. Explore new research directions. Position themselves for future leadership opportunities. The 2026 fellowship addresses this challenge by providing selected professionals with US$10,000 toward their career development. Importantly, the application itself specifically identifies conference travel, research expenses and childcare as examples of potential career-development needs. How Much Funding Is Available? Each selected 2030STEM Fellow will receive: US$10,000 toward career advancement. The 2026 call states that five STEM professionals are being sought for the fellowship. This represents a potential combined allocation of US$50,000 across the five selected Fellows, although applicants should understand that the official application describes the award individually as US$10,000 for each Fellow. What Can the US$10,000 Be Used For? The fellowship is designed around career development rather than one narrowly prescribed research project. The application specifically provides examples including: Conference Travel Funding could help a Fellow participate in professional or scientific conferences that are important for: Presenting research. Networking with collaborators. Learning about emerging developments. Meeting prospective mentors. Connecting with employers or research institutions. Building visibility within a specialist field. Research Expenses The award may also contribute to expenses associated with advancing the Fellow s research or professional work. The application does not provide an exhaustive list of eligible research costs, so applicants should explain clearly how their proposed expense will contribute to their professional advancement. Childcare One particularly notable aspect of the fellowship is the explicit recognition of childcare as a potential career-development expense. Professional travel, conferences, fieldwork and other career activities can create additional care responsibilities. By explicitly mentioning childcare, the fellowship recognizes that career barriers are not limited to laboratory or academic costs. Other Career-Development Needs The application uses the phrase “including but not limited to,” indicating that the stated examples are not necessarily the only possible uses. Applicants should therefore identify the career-development expenditure that is most relevant to their circumstances and clearly explain how the US$10,000 would produce a meaningful professional outcome. What Type of Applicants Is 2030STEM Looking For? The 2026 call specifically describes its target group as early- to mid-career STEM researchers and professionals . The strongest candidates are expected to demonstrate a history of: Building meaningful professional or scientific communities. Communicating or translating knowledge. Exercising innovative leadership. Advancing science or STEM practice. Supporting broader improvements within STEM environments. Applicants should therefore think beyond conventional achievements such as publications, degrees or job titles. The fellowship questions suggest that reviewers are interested in understanding: Where the applicant wants their career to go. What motivates their STEM career. How the applicant contributes to other people or communities. How they communicate knowledge. What kind of leadership they demonstrate. How funding would change or accelerate their career trajectory. 2030STEM s Approach to STEM Inclusion The broader mission of 2030STEM is closely connected with improving representation and opportunity across the STEM ecosystem. The organization argues that STEM institutions benefit when professionals from different backgrounds participate fully in scientific research, decision-making and leadership. Its stated work places substantial emphasis on improving opportunities for Black, Latino/a/x, Indigenous and other people of color in STEM, including by addressing structural barriers that can affect recruitment, retention, promotion, leadership and access to financial resources. However, applicants should distinguish the organization s broader mission from the formal requirements displayed on the current 2026 application form . The live 2026 form does not present a race or ethnicity field as an explicit eligibility condition. Application Requirements The 2030STEM Fellowship application requests a combination of personal details, professional information, career reflections and supporting documentation. Applicants should be prepared to provide the following. 1. Full Name Applicants must provide their first and last name. Use the same professional name that appears on your CV, publications, institutional profile and other professional records wherever possible. 2. Email Address A valid email address is required. Applicants should preferably use an email account that they monitor regularly because fellowship communications and potential follow-up regarding the selection process may be sent to this address. 3. Phone Number Applicants are required to provide a valid telephone number. 4. Highest Level of Education The application asks applicants to identify their highest completed level of education. The current 2026 form does not, within the publicly accessible text reviewed, state a specific minimum degree requirement. Applicants should therefore report their educational background accurately rather than assuming that the qualification requirements from a previous fellowship cycle automatically apply to the 2026 call. 5. Current Field or Area of Expertise Applicants must state their current field or professional area of expertise. This is an important part of establishing the applicant s connection to STEM. Applicants should use a specific description where possible. Instead of simply writing “science,” for example, an applicant may identify areas such as: Molecular biology. Environmental science. Artificial intelligence. Engineering. Chemistry. Astronomy. Biomedical research. Climate science. Data science. Mathematics. Physics. Public health research. Computer science. Scientific communication. Engineering education. The exact field should reflect the applicant s genuine professional background. 6. Current Affiliation Applicants must provide their present institutional or professional affiliation. This could potentially include a university, research institution, government entity, company, laboratory, nonprofit organization or other professional organization, depending on the applicant s circumstances. Five-Year Career Vision One of the application questions asks applicants to explain where they see themselves professionally over the next five years. Applicants are also asked to discuss: The type of science they expect to be doing. The people or types of professionals with whom they hope to collaborate. This question gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate that they have a meaningful career direction. A strong response should connect: Current position → professional development need → fellowship support → five-year objective. Applicants should avoid writing only about a desired job title. Instead, they can describe the scientific or professional impact they want to create. Explain the Pivotal Moment Behind Your STEM Career Applicants are asked to: Share a pivotal moment or experience that significantly influenced their decision to pursue their current STEM career path. This question is more personal than a conventional CV-based application question. The objective appears to be understanding the applicant s motivation, trajectory and relationship with their chosen STEM field. Applicants may consider discussing an experience such as: Exposure to an important scientific problem. A research experience. A mentor who influenced their career. A community challenge that inspired their work. An academic breakthrough. An internship or professional experience. A personal experience that led to a scientific question. A problem the applicant became determined to solve. The response should remain authentic and directly connected to the applicant s career development. Demonstrate Community Building, Knowledge Translation and Leadership This is one of the most important components of the application. Applicants must explain how they or their work have contributed to: Building community. Translating knowledge. Innovative leadership in STEM. Applicants should support their answer with concrete examples. Potential evidence may include: Creating research networks. Mentoring students or younger researchers. Leading professional groups. Developing interdisciplinary collaborations. Communicating scientific research to non-specialist audiences. Working with communities affected by scientific or technological issues. Translating research findings into policy or practice. Developing new scientific initiatives. Creating inclusive professional environments. Leading institutional changes. Developing innovative research methods or approaches. Simply describing yourself as a leader will generally be less persuasive than demonstrating what you led, who benefited and what changed. Explain How You Would Use the US$10,000 Applicants are specifically asked: If selected, how will you use the funds toward advancing your career? This response should be clear, realistic and connected with professional development. A strong answer could explain: What the funding would purchase or support. Why that particular expenditure is necessary. Why existing institutional resources cannot fully cover it, where applicable. What professional outcome the expenditure would produce. How that outcome connects with the applicant s longer-term STEM career. Applicants should avoid treating the US$10,000 simply as a financial prize. The application frames the funding specifically around career advancement . Three Professional References Are Required Applicants must provide the name and email address of three references . Importantly, the application states that references will only be contacted if the applicant progresses to the second round . Applicants should therefore select references carefully. Suitable references will generally be people who can credibly discuss the applicant s: STEM expertise. Research or professional accomplishments. Leadership. Community contributions. Collaboration. Communication skills. Professional potential. Applicants should obtain permission from references before listing their contact information and make sure the email addresses entered in the application are accurate. Resume or CV Requirement Applicants are also asked to upload a resume or curriculum vitae . The CV should reinforce the story presented throughout the application. Relevant sections could include: Education. Current position. Research experience. Professional experience. Publications. Presentations. Fellowships. Awards. Grants. Professional leadership. Community engagement. Science communication. Mentoring. Professional societies. Relevant projects. Applicants should ensure that dates, affiliations and accomplishments mentioned in their written responses are consistent with the information appearing on their CV. Additional Information Section The application concludes with an optional question asking whether there is anything else the selection team should know about the applicant . Applicants should use this space strategically. Rather than repeating information already stated elsewhere, it may be useful for providing context that is genuinely relevant to the application but has not been captured by the previous questions. How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Application The current application does not publish a numerical evaluation rubric. The following points should therefore be treated as practical application guidance rather than official scoring criteria. Demonstrate Impact, Not Only Achievement Instead of simply listing accomplishments, explain the effect of those accomplishments. For example: Who benefited? What problem was addressed? What changed? What was created? What did the applicant personally contribute? Connect Your Career Vision With the Funding The five-year career question and the funding-use question should support one another. If an applicant wants to become a leader in a particular research area, the proposed use of funding should logically move them toward that objective. Provide Evidence of Community Building Since community building is specifically mentioned by 2030STEM, applicants should identify concrete examples of how they have supported colleagues, students, professional communities or other stakeholders. Explain Knowledge Translation Knowledge translation can involve turning specialist research into information that can be understood or applied by: Policymakers. Communities. Students. Industry. Healthcare professionals. Educators. Other researchers. The general public. Applicants should demonstrate actual communication or application rather than merely saying that science communication is important. Show Innovative Leadership Leadership does not necessarily require holding a senior management position. Applicants may demonstrate leadership by initiating projects, solving problems, creating collaborations, mentoring others, changing institutional practices or introducing new scientific approaches. Previous 2030STEM Fellowship Context 2030STEM previously operated the 2030STEM × Burroughs Wellcome Fund Fellowship . The 2025 program also focused on advancing early- to mid-career STEM professionals and provided US$10,000 to Fellows. The earlier fellowship included a two-year professional-development structure involving cohort meetings, career-development workshops and access to the 2030STEM Champions network. However, these specific features are not stated on the current 2026 application form , so applicants should not assume that every condition, benefit or eligibility rule from the 2025 cycle applies automatically to the 2026 fellowship. The current application should always take precedence for the 2026 competition. Important Note About Eligibility for 2026 The archived 2025 fellowship webpage required applicants to be late-stage PhD candidates or hold a PhD or graduate equivalent such as an MD or JD, and it stated that only U.S.-based professionals would be considered. The current 2026 application form does not display those restrictions . Instead, it asks applicants to provide their highest education level, STEM field and current affiliation. Therefore, applicants should not automatically treat the archived 2025 requirements as confirmed 2026 eligibility requirements. Anyone uncertain about eligibility should rely on the current application and any additional instructions issued directly by 2030STEM. Application Deadline No application deadline is stated on the live 2030STEM Fellowship Application 2026 form reviewed on September 4, 2026. Because the organization is selecting only five Fellows, interested candidates should prepare and submit their applications promptly rather than waiting for an unconfirmed closing date. Applicants should also recheck the application page before submitting in case a deadline or additional instructions are subsequently added. How to Apply for the 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 Applicants can follow these steps: Review the fellowship description carefully. Prepare your current resume or CV. Confirm your highest educational qualification. Clearly identify your current STEM field or area of expertise. Provide your current professional or institutional affiliation. Develop a clear five-year career vision. Identify a pivotal experience that influenced your STEM career. Prepare examples demonstrating community building. Explain how you translate scientific or technical knowledge. Demonstrate innovative leadership. Develop a specific plan for using the US$10,000 award. Select three appropriate professional references. Obtain their correct names and email addresses. Complete all required sections of the online form. Upload your resume or CV. Review the application carefully. Submit the application while the form remains open. Application and reference link: Apply for the 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 The shortened reference link directs applicants to the official 2030STEM Fellowship Application 2026 hosted on Jotform. Why STEM Professionals Should Consider Applying The 2030STEM Fellowship differs from many conventional research opportunities because its focus is the professional themselves and their career advancement , rather than solely funding a tightly defined research proposal. The US$10,000 support can potentially help selected Fellows overcome practical barriers that prevent them from pursuing important professional opportunities. For an early- or mid-career STEM professional, access to funding at the right stage could help support research, participation in an important conference, collaboration-building or another strategic professional-development activity. At the same time, the application clearly signals that 2030STEM is interested in people who contribute beyond their individual technical work. Applicants who can demonstrate a combination of scientific capability, professional ambition, community engagement, communication and innovative leadership may be particularly aligned with the program s stated objectives. Application Checklist Before submitting, applicants should make sure they have: Full name. Active email address. Valid telephone number. Highest level of education. Current field or area of expertise. Current professional affiliation. A clear five-year career vision. Information about the type of science or STEM work they plan to pursue. Potential collaborators or collaboration goals. A meaningful pivotal STEM career experience. Examples of community building. Examples of knowledge translation. Examples of innovative leadership. A clear plan for using the US$10,000. Names of three references. Email addresses of all three references. Updated resume or CV. Any useful additional information not already covered elsewhere in the application. Conclusion The 2030STEM Fellowship 2026 provides an important career-development opportunity for early- to mid-career researchers and professionals seeking resources to advance their work and expand their impact within STEM. 2030STEM is selecting five Fellows , with each successful applicant receiving US$10,000 toward career advancement . Potential uses identified in the application include conference travel, research expenses, childcare and other career-development needs. The application places significant emphasis on more than academic credentials alone. Candidates are asked to demonstrate their career vision, motivation for pursuing STEM, contribution to community building, ability to translate knowledge and record of innovative leadership. Applicants are also required to explain how the US$10,000 would advance their career, provide three professional references and upload a resume or CV.
