title: HWCC Conference Travel Grants 2027: Apply for Free Registration or Up to US$1,000 to Attend the Bangkok Conference
summary: Applications are open for a limited number of travel grants supporting participation in the 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence, which will take place from March 2–4, 2027, in Bangkok, Thailand. Successful applicants may receive either a conference registration fee waiver or financial assistance of US$500 or US$1,000 toward travel costs. Applicants can request only one of these three support options. The application window runs from September 1 to October 31, 2026. All applications must be submitted in English through the official online form by 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026 . Applicants are expected to receive the outcome of their applications by November 15, 2026. The official travel-grant page confirms the deadline, support options and priority criteria . Travel Grant Opportunity at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity name Travel Support for the 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence Conference dates March 2–4, 2027 Location Bangkok, Thailand Venue Avani+ Riverside Bangkok Hotel Application opening date September 1, 2026 Application deadline October 31, 2026, at 23:59 GMT Notification date By November 15, 2026 Application language English Available support Registration waiver or reimbursement, US$500 toward travel, or US$1,000 toward travel Number of options allowed Applicants may request only one support option Conference registration required before applying No Application method Online Google application form Host IUCN SSC Human-Wildlife Conflict Coexistence Specialist Group About the 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence The 2nd International Conference on Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence will bring together people working across conservation, research, policy, development, agriculture, technology and community-based practice. Human-wildlife conflict can occur when interactions between people and wildlife create actual or perceived negative consequences for human livelihoods, safety, well-being, conservation objectives or animal welfare. Addressing these challenges requires more than biological research. It frequently involves community participation, governance, economic incentives, land-use planning, communication, behavioral science, conflict resolution and public policy. The conference is being organized by the IUCN Species Survival Commission’s Human-Wildlife Conflict and Coexistence Specialist Group. It will build on the first international conference, held in Oxford in 2023, which brought together nearly 600 participants from 70 countries and all continents. The second conference will be held over three days in Bangkok from March 2–4, 2027. It is expected to convene Indigenous and local community leaders, conservation practitioners, researchers, government representatives, grant-makers, policymakers and professionals from other relevant sectors. The official conference overview explains its international, cross-sectoral focus . Main Objectives of the Conference The conference aims to improve international cooperation and learning on human-wildlife conflict and coexistence. Its stated objectives include: Promoting a shared understanding of human-wildlife conflict and coexistence through new perspectives, scientific knowledge, practical insights and technological advances. Supporting the development of frameworks and approaches that improve research, management and mitigation. Encouraging approaches that can influence national and international policies concerning human-wildlife conflict. Facilitating dialogue and learning between different professional sectors and academic disciplines. Examining emerging dimensions of human-wildlife conflict and coexistence. Supporting local, national and international collaboration between practitioners, policymakers, researchers, communities and other stakeholders. Advancing interdisciplinary approaches that consider the ecological, social, economic, cultural, political and behavioral dimensions of human-wildlife interactions. The event is intended to provide a platform for practical discussion, knowledge exchange, professional networking and the development of new collaborations. What Support Is Available? Applicants must select only one of the following three options in the application form. Option 1: Free Conference Registration Successful applicants under this option will have their conference registration fee waived. The organizers will send successful recipients a registration form so that they can register and confirm their place at the conference. If a successful applicant has already registered and paid for a conference ticket, the organizers state that the ticket cost will be reimbursed. This option may be useful for applicants who can arrange their own transportation and accommodation but cannot afford the conference registration fee. Option 2: US$500 Toward Travel Costs Applicants may request US$500 toward the costs of travelling to Bangkok. The official page states that successful recipients will receive the amount in cash and in person at the conference on March 3, 2027. The webpage does not state that the organizers will purchase airline tickets, reserve accommodation or provide the US$500 before the conference. Applicants should therefore plan on arranging and initially financing their travel unless their award letter expressly states otherwise. Option 3: US$1,000 Toward Travel Costs Applicants from eligible locations may request US$1,000 toward travel expenses. As with the US$500 option, the amount will be provided in cash and in person at the conference in Bangkok on March 3, 2027. The award letter issued to each successful applicant will confirm the payment arrangement. The US$1,000 option is not available to applicants based in: Bangladesh Bhutan Brunei Cambodia China India Indonesia Laos Malaysia Maldives Myanmar Nepal Philippines Singapore Sri Lanka Taiwan Thailand Vietnam Applicants from these locations may still select the free conference registration option or the US$500 travel-support option, provided they otherwise satisfy the requirements. Important Funding Limitation The travel-grant programme is not described as full sponsorship. Applicants should understand the following points: Only a limited number of awards are available. Submitting an application does not guarantee funding. Applicants may request only one support option. A US$500 or US$1,000 travel award is not described as including free conference registration. A registration waiver is not described as including airfare, accommodation or other travel expenses. The travel money is scheduled to be distributed in person on March 3, 2027. The webpage does not promise advance payment or direct flight booking. The webpage does not specify whether visa costs, accommodation, insurance or local transportation qualify as travel expenses. The final award letter will confirm the arrangement offered to each recipient. Applicants should prepare a realistic financial plan covering any costs not included in their selected support option. A Critical Cash-Flow Consideration The timing of the travel-grant payment is particularly important. The main conference starts on March 2, 2027, while the US$500 or US$1,000 award is scheduled to be paid in person on March 3, 2027. This means recipients may need to purchase their tickets, obtain a visa, arrange insurance, book accommodation and reach Bangkok before receiving the money. Applicants should not assume that selection will remove the need for advance funds. Before accepting an award, recipients should confirm: Whether they must purchase their own airline ticket. Whether any payment can be made before departure. Whether the award may be used for accommodation. Whether proof of expenditure will be required. Whether conference registration must be purchased separately. Whether payment will be made in U.S. dollars or an equivalent local currency. Whether identification or a signed receipt will be required to collect the cash. What happens if the recipient experiences a visa refusal or travel disruption. Unless the award letter states otherwise, applicants should treat the funding as a contribution toward attendance rather than complete coverage of every cost. Who Receives Priority? The official page does not state that applicants must meet every priority criterion. It says priority will be given to applicants who meet any of the following: Residents of countries not classified as high-income under the World Bank country classification. Students from any country. Applicants who submitted an abstract for a talk, poster or session. Individuals included in a conference session submitted by another person. These are priority factors rather than clearly stated absolute eligibility restrictions. Therefore, the published information does not explicitly exclude: Non-students. Applicants from high-income countries. Applicants who did not submit an abstract. Applicants who are not presenting at the conference. People working outside universities. Independent practitioners and consultants. Private-sector professionals. Government employees. Members of nonprofit or intergovernmental organizations. However, applicants who do not meet any priority criterion may face stronger competition because the available funding is limited. Do Applicants Need to Register for the Conference First? No. Applicants do not need to register for the conference before submitting a travel-support application. This is important because one of the available options is a registration fee waiver. Applicants seeking this option do not need to pay the registration fee merely to qualify for consideration. Those who have already purchased a ticket may still apply. If they are selected for the registration-support option, the organizers state that the ticket will be reimbursed. Applicants should keep their: Registration confirmation. Payment receipt. Invoice. Card or bank transaction record. Any correspondence with the conference organizer. These records may be needed to arrange reimbursement. Status of the Call for Contributions The conference’s separate call for abstracts and session contributions closed on August 31, 2026. The travel-grant application opened on September 1, 2026. Consequently, applicants who submitted an abstract, poster, talk or session proposal before the contributions deadline may receive priority during travel-grant consideration. Someone who did not submit a contribution may still apply for travel assistance because submitting an abstract is not stated as a mandatory requirement. However, the person cannot now rely on that particular priority factor unless the organizers reopen the contributions process. The conference accepted proposals across a broad range of subjects, including: Human, cultural and behavioral dimensions of coexistence. Landscape-scale, climate and ecological issues. Development, livelihoods, food security, poverty and well-being. Communications and media. Technology, artificial intelligence and scientific innovation. Compensation, insurance, incentives and other financial instruments. Practical conflict resolution and peacebuilding. Policy and governance. Connections between science and policy. Lived experience and traditional knowledge. One Health approaches. Animal behavior, ethics and animal welfare. The contribution formats included symposia, panels, reverse panels, interactive sessions, workshops, film screenings, individual presentations, speed talks and posters. The official contribution page confirms that submissions are now closed . Application Form Requirements The official application form is relatively short. It currently requests the following information: Personal and contact information Applicants must provide: First and last name. Email address. Main country of residence. Employment and affiliation Applicants must identify the type of organization with which they work. The form provides the following options: Government. Private sector. NGO or nonprofit organization. Intergovernmental organization. Academia or research institution. Independent or consultancy. Other. Applicants must also state their organization or professional affiliation. Student status The application asks whether the applicant is currently a student. Students from any country are one of the groups given priority, but the form also allows non-students to apply. Conference contribution status Applicants must state whether they submitted an abstract to the conference. The form also asks whether they have been included as a panelist or speaker in a proposal submitted by another person. Available responses are: Yes. No. I do not know. Funding justification statement Applicants must respond to the following substantive question in no more than 150 words: Explain how attending the conference will further your work in human-wildlife conflict and coexistence and why you need financial support to attend. This is the main written justification on the current form. Applicants should use the limited word count carefully. Requested grant option Applicants must choose one of the following: Free conference registration. US$500 toward travel costs. US$1,000 toward travel costs, where geographically available. The current form does not display a requirement to upload a curriculum vitae, passport, recommendation letter, academic transcript, detailed budget or copy of an abstract. Applicants should nevertheless recheck the live form before submission in case the organizers make changes. How to Write a Strong 150-Word Funding Statement The 150-word response should address both parts of the question: How attending will advance the applicant’s work. Why the applicant cannot attend without financial assistance. A practical structure could be: Opening: Professional or community context Briefly introduce your work and the human-wildlife conflict issue you address. For example, explain whether you work in conservation, research, agriculture, public policy, local government, community development, animal welfare, livelihoods or another related area. Current challenge Identify the specific problem, knowledge gap or implementation challenge affecting your work. Avoid relying only on broad statements such as “human-wildlife conflict is important.” Describe the particular problem your community, institution or project is facing. Value of conference participation Explain how the conference will help you: Learn a specific approach. Connect with relevant specialists. improve an existing intervention. Strengthen policy development. Develop a collaboration. Share community knowledge. Apply research findings. Bring practical lessons back to your institution or community. Financial need State clearly why assistance is necessary. Where relevant, mention limited institutional funding, student status, unfavorable exchange rates, long-distance travel costs or lack of access to professional-development funding. Applicants should remain factual and avoid making unsupported claims. Suggested 150-Word Allocation Applicants may use the following approximate structure: 30–40 words: Your role and the human-wildlife issue you address. 35–45 words: The practical problem or knowledge gap affecting your work. 40–50 words: How conference learning and connections will improve your work. 20–30 words: Why financial support is necessary. 10–20 words: The outcome you intend to deliver after returning. What Conference Registration Includes According to the registration page, the main conference registration fee includes: Access to sessions in the main conference programme. Tea, coffee and snacks twice each day. Lunch on all three conference days. Admission to the conference reception. The following are optional or separately ticketed: Conference dinner. Pre-conference short courses. Other separately advertised activities. Registration does not automatically cover international travel, accommodation, visas, insurance or other personal expenses. The official registration page explains what the ticket includes . Visa, Passport and Insurance Responsibilities International participants are responsible for checking the entry requirements that apply to their nationality and travel documents. Delegates should plan for: A passport valid for the required period. A Thai visa or electronic visa where applicable. Thailand’s entry and arrival requirements. Travel and health insurance. Cancellation insurance where appropriate. Vaccination or health documentation if required. Sufficient funds for accommodation and daily expenses. Contingency costs caused by delays or cancellations. Thailand requires international visitors to complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card before arrival. Entry rules can change, so selected applicants should verify requirements through official Thai government sources before booking travel. Decide which single support option best matches your financial situation. Open the official travel-grant application form . Enter your name, email address and main country of residence. Select your organization type. Provide your institutional or professional affiliation. Confirm whether you are a student. State whether you submitted a conference abstract. State whether you are included as a speaker or panelist in someone else’s proposal. Prepare a focused statement of no more than 150 words. Select only one grant option. Review every response carefully. Submit the form before 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026. Save evidence that the form was submitted. Monitor your email, including spam and junk folders, for the outcome. Google sign-in is offered as a way to save application progress. Applicants should still prepare the 150-word response in a separate document before entering it into the form. Application Preparation Checklist Before starting the online application, prepare: Your name exactly as used in professional correspondence. A reliable email address. Your country of residence. The name of your employer, university, organization or professional affiliation. Your organization type. Confirmation of your current student status. Details of any conference abstract or session proposal. Confirmation from a session organizer if you may have been included as a speaker. A 150-word funding justification. A realistic estimate of your overall attendance costs. A decision on which one of the three support options to request. A plan for financing travel before the in-person payment date, if requesting travel funding. Practical Tips for Applicants Choose the appropriate grant option Do not automatically select the highest amount. If you can fund your travel but cannot afford conference registration, the registration waiver may be the most suitable request. If you need help with airfare or another travel cost, select either US$500 or US$1,000, subject to the geographical restriction on the US$1,000 option. Address both elements of the main question A response that only explains your professional work is incomplete. You must also explain why you need funding. Similarly, a response that discusses only financial hardship without demonstrating a meaningful connection to the conference may be less persuasive. Emphasize a practical post-conference outcome Explain what you will do with the knowledge and contacts gained. Examples could include: Updating a community conflict-management programme. Sharing lessons with colleagues. Improving a research method. Developing a policy recommendation. Organizing a local training session. Strengthening a cross-border collaboration. Integrating community perspectives into a conservation programme. Do not assume the grant is paid before travel The official payment arrangement states that travel-grant recipients will receive cash in Bangkok on March 3, 2027. Prepare accordingly. Submit early The deadline is fixed at 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026. Submitting early gives applicants time to address internet, form or email problems. Keep the statement within 150 words Exceeding the maximum length may weaken the application or result in text being cut off. Draft and count the words before pasting the response into the form. Travel-Grant Sponsors The sponsor logos displayed on the official page identify: Fondation Segré. Golden Triangle Asian Elephant Foundation. The conference is organized by the IUCN SSC Human-Wildlife Conflict Coexistence Specialist Group. Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture travel grants. These are separate programmes with their own eligibility rules, application procedures and deadlines. Conclusion The 2027 HWCC Conference travel-support programme provides an important opportunity for people working on human-wildlife conflict and coexistence to participate in an international gathering in Bangkok. Applicants can request one of three forms of support: free conference registration, US$500 toward travel expenses or US$1,000 toward travel expenses. Priority will be given to residents of countries not classified as high-income, students and people contributing to the conference programme, but the published information does not restrict applications exclusively to these groups. Applicants should carefully consider the payment arrangement before applying. Travel awards are scheduled to be paid in cash at the conference on March 3, 2027, rather than before departure. The main application requirement is a concise 150-word explanation of how conference participation will advance the applicant’s work and why financial assistance is needed. Clear, specific and honest responses will be more effective than broad descriptions of conservation challenges. Applications must be submitted in English through the official online form by 23:59 GMT on October 31, 2026 . Applicants are expected to receive the outcome by November 15, 2026. title: EAC Youth Fellowship 2026: Fully Develop Your Leadership Skills, Build Regional Networks and Champion East African Integration
summary: The EAC Youth Fellowship is a leadership development opportunity designed to empower young people across East Africa to become active contributors to regional integration, cooperation and sustainable development. The fellowship focuses on nurturing the next generation of East African leaders by providing young professionals with opportunities for mentorship, leadership development, capacity building and regional networking. The initiative brings together emerging leaders from countries within the East African Community (EAC) and provides a platform for young people to strengthen their understanding of regional integration while developing the skills, relationships and confidence needed to create meaningful impact. The 4th Cohort of the EAC Youth Fellowship is currently open for applications. Eligible young people between the ages of 18 and 35 who hold at least a bachelor s degree and demonstrate strong leadership potential are encouraged to apply. About the EAC Youth Fellowship The EAC Youth Fellowship is an initiative focused on engaging and empowering young people in the development and integration of the East African region. The fellowship recognizes that young people represent an important source of ideas, leadership, innovation and community-level action. As East Africa continues to experience economic, social, political and technological transformation, young leaders have an increasingly important role to play in shaping the region s future. The programme therefore seeks to provide young people with opportunities to understand regional issues, develop leadership capabilities, establish professional relationships and participate more meaningfully in regional development. The fellowship is built around the broader goal of nurturing the next generation of East African leaders . Through its activities, participants can strengthen their capacity in areas related to: Leadership Regional integration Policy understanding Economic governance Business Community development Regional cooperation Professional networking Social transformation The fellowship is supported by the Danida Fellowship Centre and MS TCDC , with MS TCDC serving as a Pan-African training centre based in Arusha, Tanzania. What Is the Purpose of the EAC Youth Fellowship? The EAC Youth Fellowship seeks to ensure that young people are not simply beneficiaries of regional development but active participants in shaping the future of East Africa. The programme provides a platform through which young leaders can develop the knowledge and relationships necessary to engage with regional challenges and opportunities. Its objectives include: Developing young leaders who can contribute to regional transformation. Strengthening understanding of EAC regional integration and related development processes. Building professional and leadership networks among young people from across East Africa. Providing mentorship from experienced professionals and leaders. Improving participants leadership skills through training, workshops and seminars. Encouraging youth participation in regional development and cooperation. Connecting young leaders with policymakers and professionals working across the EAC region. The fellowship therefore goes beyond conventional leadership training by creating opportunities for participants to build relationships across national borders. Who Can Apply for the EAC Youth Fellowship? The EAC Youth Fellowship has clearly defined eligibility requirements concerning age, nationality or country of residence, education and leadership potential. Applicants should carefully review each requirement before submitting an application. Age Requirement Applicants must be between 18 and 35 years old . This means the fellowship is targeted at young adults and emerging professionals who are at an important stage of developing their leadership careers and professional contributions. The age requirement creates an opportunity for both younger graduates beginning their professional journeys and more experienced young professionals who are already leading initiatives or contributing to their communities. Eligible Countries The fellowship is open to young people from the following eight countries: Kenya Tanzania Uganda South Sudan Burundi Rwanda Somalia Democratic Republic of the Congo Applicants must therefore come from one of these eligible East African countries. The geographic scope of the programme makes it particularly relevant to young professionals interested in strengthening connections and cooperation across the East African region. Educational Requirement Applicants must hold at least a Bachelor s degree or its equivalent . This means the fellowship is designed primarily for graduates who have completed undergraduate-level education or an equivalent qualification. In addition to the minimum bachelor s degree requirement, the programme indicates that additional qualifications related to relevant fields are highly valued. These may include qualifications or academic backgrounds connected to: Regional integration Leadership Business Economic governance Related fields Applicants whose academic or professional backgrounds align with these areas may therefore be particularly well positioned to demonstrate their suitability for the programme. Leadership Potential A bachelor s degree alone is not sufficient. Applicants must also demonstrate strong leadership potential . This is an important component of the fellowship because the programme is designed to nurture individuals who can contribute to the future development and integration of East Africa. Leadership potential can be demonstrated through experiences such as: Leading a community initiative Coordinating a youth organization Managing a project Participating in civic activities Supporting social development programmes Leading professional or academic activities Organizing community events Contributing to policy-related activities Building networks or partnerships Creating solutions to community challenges Applicants should focus on demonstrating the impact and responsibility associated with their leadership experiences rather than simply listing positions or titles. What Are the Benefits of the EAC Youth Fellowship? Selected fellows will receive access to a range of leadership development and professional networking opportunities. The fellowship s main benefits include mentorship, regional networking and leadership development. 1. Mentorship Opportunities One of the central benefits of the EAC Youth Fellowship is access to experienced mentors. Fellows will have opportunities to engage with mentors who can provide guidance, support and apprenticeship throughout the fellowship. Mentorship can help emerging leaders gain practical insights that are difficult to obtain solely through academic study. Through interaction with experienced professionals, fellows can potentially develop a better understanding of: Leadership challenges Professional development Regional development Career planning Decision-making Project implementation Stakeholder engagement Leadership responsibility The mentorship component is particularly valuable for young professionals who want to strengthen both their leadership capacity and their professional networks. 2. Regional Professional Networks The fellowship provides participants with access to a network of professionals, policymakers and young leaders from across the EAC region. This regional networking component is one of the distinctive features of the programme. Instead of developing professional relationships only within their own countries, fellows can connect with individuals working across different East African contexts. These connections can facilitate: Cross-border collaboration Knowledge exchange Professional partnerships Regional projects Peer learning Leadership opportunities Exposure to different perspectives For young professionals interested in regional integration, international development or African leadership, building these relationships can be particularly valuable. 3. Leadership Development Fellows will participate in workshops, training sessions and seminars designed to enhance their leadership capabilities. The leadership development component focuses on strengthening participants abilities to understand complex issues, engage with stakeholders and contribute to regional development. Training activities may help fellows strengthen their understanding of: Leadership Policy Regional integration Governance Development Professional collaboration Strategic thinking The programme therefore combines networking with structured learning and leadership development. Understanding Regional Integration A key theme of the EAC Youth Fellowship is regional integration . Regional integration involves countries working together to improve cooperation and address shared challenges. For East Africa, regional cooperation can involve areas such as: Trade Economic development Infrastructure Education Mobility Health Governance Environmental sustainability Peace and security Youth development Innovation Young leaders who understand these interconnected issues can contribute more effectively to initiatives that extend beyond national boundaries. The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity for participants to develop a broader perspective on the region and understand how developments in one country can affect others. Why Youth Leadership Matters in East Africa East Africa has one of the world s youngest populations, making youth participation particularly important to the region s future. Young people are already contributing to their communities through entrepreneurship, social innovation, civil society, research, technology, education and public service. However, young leaders often need access to: Professional networks Mentorship Leadership training Policy knowledge Regional platforms Opportunities for collaboration The EAC Youth Fellowship seeks to address some of these needs by connecting emerging leaders with peers, mentors, professionals and policymakers from across the region. The programme can therefore help young people move from local leadership toward broader regional engagement. What Kind of Applicants May Benefit Most? Although the fellowship is open to eligible applicants across several professional backgrounds, it may be particularly relevant to young people whose interests or careers intersect with regional development. Potentially relevant backgrounds include: Young Professionals Professionals between 18 and 35 who are seeking to strengthen their leadership capabilities and regional networks can benefit from the programme. Community Leaders Young people already leading community initiatives can use the fellowship to expand their understanding of regional development and connect with other changemakers. Policy and Governance Professionals Individuals working or aspiring to work in public policy, governance or economic development may find the programme particularly relevant because of its focus on policy understanding and regional integration. Entrepreneurs and Business Professionals Young entrepreneurs and business professionals interested in East African markets and regional cooperation may benefit from exposure to professionals from across the EAC. Researchers and Academics Graduates and researchers working on topics connected to regional integration, governance, economics, development or leadership may also find the fellowship relevant. Civil Society and Development Practitioners Young professionals working with NGOs, civil society organizations and development initiatives can potentially use the fellowship to strengthen their leadership and regional networks. What Makes the EAC Youth Fellowship Valuable? The fellowship combines three elements that are particularly important for emerging leaders: Mentorship + Leadership Development + Regional Networking Many leadership programmes focus primarily on training. The EAC Youth Fellowship goes further by creating opportunities for participants to establish relationships with other young leaders and experienced professionals. This combination can help participants develop both knowledge and social capital. For example, a fellow may learn about regional policy through a workshop, discuss the issue with an experienced mentor and then connect with another participant working on a related challenge in a different East African country. Such interactions can create opportunities for long-term collaboration beyond the fellowship itself. Demonstrate Leadership Experience Applicants should clearly explain how they have demonstrated leadership. Rather than simply stating that they have held a leadership position, applicants should describe: What they led The problem they addressed Who benefited What actions they took What results were achieved What they learned Specific examples are generally more compelling than broad statements. 2. Explain Your Interest in East Africa Because the programme focuses on regional integration, applicants should be able to explain why East African cooperation matters to them. Consider discussing: A regional challenge you care about Your experience working across communities or countries Your interest in EAC integration How your career relates to regional development How you want to contribute to East Africa 3. Connect Your Education to Your Goals Applicants should demonstrate how their bachelor s degree or equivalent qualification has prepared them for the fellowship. If you have additional qualifications related to leadership, business, economic governance or regional integration, explain how these qualifications support your professional goals. 4. Highlight Your Future Leadership Potential The fellowship is not only concerned with what applicants have already accomplished. Applicants should also demonstrate where they want to go. Explain: The type of leader you want to become The issues you want to address The communities you want to serve How regional networks could support your goals How you intend to contribute to East Africa 5. Emphasize Collaboration Regional leadership requires the ability to work with people from different countries, cultures and professional backgrounds. Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they value: Collaboration Diversity Cross-cultural learning Dialogue Partnership Knowledge sharing How to Apply for the EAC Youth Fellowship Applications for the 4th Cohort of the EAC Youth Fellowship are submitted through the designated online application platform. The programme does not include certificate qualifications or PhD programmes. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to students seeking to build academic and professional careers in areas associated with disaster preparedness, disaster risk reduction, emergency management, fire safety, fire technology, fire engineering and related areas. What Is the NDMC Bursary? The NDMC Bursary Programme is an educational funding opportunity administered through the National Disaster Management Centre under the Department of Cooperative Governance. The programme is designed around academic programmes relevant to disaster management and fire-related disciplines. By supporting students in these fields, the initiative seeks to contribute to the development of individuals with the knowledge and skills required in areas connected to disaster management and fire services. Applicants should therefore ensure that their intended qualification is directly aligned with one of the fields specified in the bursary advertisement before submitting an application. Fields of Study Covered The 2027 NDMC bursary focuses on qualifications in the following broad study areas: 1. Disaster Management Students interested in disaster management may consider eligible programmes dealing with areas such as disaster risk reduction, disaster preparedness, emergency management, disaster response, recovery, resilience and related disaster management disciplines. Applicants should verify that their specific programme is recognised as a qualifying Disaster Management qualification under the bursary requirements. 2. Fire Technology The bursary also welcomes qualifying students pursuing Fire Technology programmes. Fire Technology is relevant to the technical and operational aspects of fire prevention, fire protection and fire-related safety systems. Students interested in this area should confirm that their chosen qualification meets the NDMC s requirements. 3. Fire Engineering Students pursuing qualifying Fire Engineering programmes may also apply. Fire Engineering involves technical and engineering approaches to fire safety, fire prevention, fire protection and related areas. As with the other fields, applicants should ensure that their qualification is offered by a recognised public higher education institution in South Africa and meets the requirements of the bursary programme. Qualifications Covered by the Bursary The NDMC states that applicants may pursue several levels of qualification during the 2027 academic year. These include: Undergraduate programmes Post-Graduate Diploma programmes Advanced Diploma programmes Full Master s programmes However, there are important exclusions. The bursary does not cover: Certificate qualifications PhD qualifications Applicants considering programmes outside the listed qualification levels should carefully check the official bursary advertisement before applying. Minimum Academic Requirements Academic performance is an important requirement for the 2027 NDMC Bursary Programme. Applicants must provide their most recent academic results, statement of results or academic transcript. The stated minimum averages are: Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants Applicants for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma programmes must have a minimum average of 60% . Master s applicants Applicants applying for Master s-level study must have a minimum average of 65% . This means prospective applicants should carefully review their latest academic results before beginning the application process. Meeting the minimum academic average does not necessarily guarantee selection, as applicants must also satisfy the other requirements of the bursary programme and provide all requested documentation. Supporting Documents Required Applicants are required to submit supporting documentation together with their bursary application. The NDMC application system specifies the documents that should be attached and downloaded underneath the application form in the required sequence. Applicants should prepare the following documents: 1. Certified Copy of South African Identity Document Applicants must provide a certified copy of their South African Identity Document . The document should meet the certification requirements specified for the application. Prospective applicants should make sure that the copy is clear and legible before uploading it. 2. Certified Copy of Matric Certificate A certified copy of the applicant s Matric Certificate is also required. Applicants should ensure that the document is properly certified and that all relevant information can be clearly read. 3. Most Recent Academic Results Applicants must provide their most recent academic results, statement of results or academic transcript . This document is particularly important because the NDMC specifies minimum academic averages for different qualification levels. The requirement is: 60% minimum average for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants. 65% minimum average for Master s applicants. Applicants should therefore submit their most recent available academic record. 4. Proof of Application, Acceptance or Registration Applicants must also provide proof of application, acceptance or registration . This document should demonstrate the applicant s status with the relevant higher education institution. Depending on the applicant s circumstances, this may be proof that they have applied to, been accepted by, or registered with the relevant institution. Applicants should make sure that the document clearly identifies the institution and the relevant programme. 5. Curriculum Vitae for Master s Applicants Master s applicants are required to provide a brief Curriculum Vitae (CV) . The CV must be no longer than two pages . This requirement specifically applies to Master s applicants, so applicants at other qualification levels should pay attention to the distinction in the application requirements. A concise CV should focus on relevant academic background, experience, skills, achievements and other information that may demonstrate the applicant s suitability for postgraduate study. 6. Master s Research Proposal Applicants applying for Master s programmes must also submit a research proposal . The research proposal must focus on one of the 16 Priority Thematic Areas identified by the NDMC. This is an important requirement for Master s applicants and should not be overlooked. Applicants should review the official research agenda and ensure that their proposed research topic falls within one of the specified priority thematic areas. 16 Priority Thematic Areas for Master s Research Master s applicants are required to develop their research proposal around one of the NDMC s 16 Priority Thematic Areas . Prospective Master s students should therefore review the official research agenda before preparing their proposal. The research agenda is available through the NDMC bursary application system and should be consulted carefully to understand the priority areas and ensure that the proposed research is appropriately aligned. Applicants can access the NDMC Research Agenda through the official application system s research agenda document. Where Can Successful Applicants Study? The bursary is intended for qualifying programmes offered at a recognised Public Higher Institution of South Africa . Applicants should therefore pay close attention to the type of institution they intend to attend. The information provided by the NDMC specifically refers to recognised public higher education institutions in South Africa. Students should verify the status of their institution and programme before submitting an application. Important Application Deadline The deadline for the 2027 NDMC Bursary application has been updated. Application deadline: 30 September 2026 at 23:59. Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their applications. Preparing documents such as certified identification, Matric certificates, academic transcripts, proof of university application or registration and, where applicable, a Master s research proposal can take time. It is therefore advisable to begin the application process early and ensure that all required documents have been correctly prepared and uploaded before the deadline. Important: The Application System Does Not Support Mobile Devices One of the most important technical instructions provided by the NDMC is that the application system does not support mobile devices . The notice specifically states that the system does not support: Android devices Apple devices Applicants should therefore avoid relying on a smartphone or tablet to complete their application. Instead, applicants should use a desktop or laptop computer to access and complete the online application. This is particularly important because attempting to submit an application through an unsupported device could result in technical difficulties or prevent the applicant from completing the process successfully. How to Apply for the 2027 NDMC Bursary Applicants who meet the requirements can apply through the NDMC Bursary Management System. Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility Before beginning the application, confirm that: You are applying for the 2027 academic year. Your intended programme is in Disaster Management, Fire Technology or Fire Engineering. Your qualification falls within the eligible qualification levels. Your institution is a recognised public higher education institution in South Africa. You meet the applicable academic average requirement. You have the required supporting documentation. Step 2: Prepare Your Supporting Documents Prepare the required documents before starting the online application. These include: Certified South African Identity Document. Certified Matric Certificate. Most recent academic results, statement or transcript. Proof of application, acceptance or registration. Two-page maximum CV for Master s applicants. Master s research proposal aligned with one of the 16 Priority Thematic Areas, where applicable. Having the documents ready in advance can make the application process easier and reduce the risk of submitting an incomplete application. Step 3: Access the NDMC Bursary Application System Applications are submitted online through the NDMC Bursary Management System . Applicants should use a supported computer rather than an Android or Apple mobile device. Step 4: Complete the Application Form Applicants should provide accurate information when completing the online application. Make sure that information entered into the application corresponds with the information contained in the supporting documents. Step 5: Upload the Required Documents Upload the requested supporting documents according to the instructions provided by the NDMC. Applicants should check that: Documents are clear and readable. Certified copies are properly certified. The correct academic record has been provided. Proof of application, acceptance or registration is included. Master s applicants include their CV and research proposal. All required attachments have been submitted. Step 6: Submit Before the Deadline Once the application has been completed and all supporting documents have been uploaded, submit it before: 30 September 2026 at 23:59. Applicants should avoid leaving submission until the last minute because technical problems, internet connectivity issues or missing documents could prevent timely submission. Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity is particularly relevant to students who are planning to build academic and professional careers in disaster management, fire technology or fire engineering. It may be suitable for: Students pursuing eligible Undergraduate qualifications. Students pursuing eligible Post-Graduate Diplomas. Students pursuing eligible Advanced Diplomas. Students pursuing eligible Master s programmes. Students interested in disaster management and related disciplines. Students interested in fire technology. Students interested in fire engineering. Master s applicants whose proposed research can be aligned with one of the NDMC s 16 Priority Thematic Areas. Applicants should nevertheless review the complete official requirements before applying. Why This Opportunity Is Important Disaster management and fire-related fields play an important role in protecting communities, infrastructure and public safety. Training professionals in these disciplines can contribute to areas such as: Disaster preparedness Disaster risk reduction Emergency planning Disaster response Recovery and resilience Fire prevention Fire safety Fire protection Fire engineering Public safety Risk management For students interested in these areas, pursuing a relevant qualification can provide an opportunity to develop specialised knowledge that can be applied in government, emergency services, disaster management structures, fire services, private organisations, research institutions and other related sectors. Tips for a Strong NDMC Bursary Application Applicants can take several practical steps to reduce avoidable mistakes. Check your academic average Make sure your latest academic results meet the relevant threshold before applying. Remember: 60% minimum for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants. 65% minimum for Master s applicants. Verify your programme Do not assume that every programme with a similar title will automatically qualify. Confirm that your intended programme falls within the specified areas of Disaster Management, Fire Technology or Fire Engineering. Prepare certified documents early Certification can take time, particularly when several documents are required. Prepare your certified copies well before the deadline. Master s applicants should start their research proposal early A Master s research proposal requires considerably more preparation than simply completing an online form. Applicants should first review the 16 Priority Thematic Areas and then develop a research proposal that clearly aligns with one of them. Keep the Master s CV within the required length The NDMC specifies a maximum of two pages for the Master s applicant CV. Avoid submitting an unnecessarily long CV. Use a computer Because the application system does not support Android or Apple mobile devices, applicants should complete the application using a suitable desktop or laptop computer. Do not wait until the final hours The deadline is 30 September 2026 at 23:59 . Submitting early gives applicants more time to address technical issues or correct missing information. Applicants must also meet the applicable academic requirements, with a minimum average of 60% for Undergraduate, Post-Graduate Diploma and Advanced Diploma applicants and 65% for Master s applicants. Master s applicants have additional requirements, including a maximum two-page CV and a research proposal based on one of the NDMC s 16 Priority Thematic Areas. title: Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship in the Humanities 2027–28 at Simon Fraser University: Eligibility, Benefits, Application Process and Deadline
summary: The Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship in the Humanities 2027–28 at Simon Fraser University (SFU) is now accepting applications from emerging and established academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers working in the humanities and arts. Hosted by the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences (FASS) at Simon Fraser University in British Columbia, Canada, the fellowship provides an opportunity for talented and engaged individuals to develop a meaningful project within an academic and intellectual environment. The fellowship supports creative practice and publicly engaged scholarship while encouraging applicants to explore major concerns affecting society and contribute to conversations around decolonization, Indigenization, culture, creativity and social change. For scholars, artists, writers, knowledge keepers and practitioners whose work connects intellectual inquiry with creative practice or public engagement, the Shadbolt Fellowship offers an opportunity to develop an important project while becoming part of the Simon Fraser University community. About the Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship The Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship in the Humanities is supported by the Jack and Doris Shadbolt Endowment for the Humanities. The fellowship reflects the vision of Jack and Doris Shadbolt, who viewed the humanities and arts as deeply connected to the natural and social worlds inhabited by artists, scholars and thinkers. The programme seeks to promote the humanities and arts as important sites of: Creative practice Critical engagement Public scholarship Cultural reflection Intellectual inquiry Social engagement Decolonization Indigenization Creative world-making Engagement with major concerns of contemporary society Rather than restricting the fellowship to traditional academic research, SFU takes a broad approach to the humanities and arts. Potential fellows may be academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners or writers. This makes the opportunity relevant to individuals working across a wide range of intellectual, artistic, cultural and publicly engaged fields. 2027–28 Fellowship Opportunity The Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences at Simon Fraser University is inviting applications for the 2027–28 academic year. Applicants are expected to propose a project that they intend to undertake during the fellowship. The proposed project should be clearly explained and demonstrate why the applicant s work would benefit from a fellowship at Simon Fraser University. Applicants should clearly communicate: The project they intend to undertake. The purpose and importance of the project. What they hope to accomplish during the fellowship. How the project relates to the humanities and/or arts. Their preferred primary unit affiliation within FASS. Any desired secondary affiliation within SFU. The length of fellowship they are requesting. Why the requested fellowship duration is appropriate for the project. Who Can Apply? The Shadbolt Fellowship is intended for emerging or established engaged academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers in the humanities and arts. Potential applicants may include people whose work involves: Humanities research Arts and creative practice Writing Cultural knowledge Public scholarship Community-based intellectual work Creative research Socially engaged artistic practice Critical humanities scholarship Indigenous knowledge and cultural practice Interdisciplinary humanities and arts projects Publicly engaged research and creative work The fellowship is therefore not limited exclusively to conventional university academics. Emerging Applicants The programme welcomes emerging scholars, artists, writers, practitioners and knowledge keepers. Applicants who are at an earlier stage of their careers may be considered if they have a strong project and demonstrate the experience and preparation necessary to undertake it. Established Applicants Established scholars, artists, practitioners, writers and knowledge keepers are also eligible to apply. The programme seeks a diverse group of resident fellows representing different stages of professional and intellectual development. International Applicants The official announcement does not specify a nationality or citizenship restriction. Therefore, the opportunity is not presented as being limited to Canadian citizens or residents. Applicants from outside Canada may apply if they satisfy the fellowship s eligibility requirements and are suitable candidates. This means applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, the Caribbean, Oceania and other regions may consider applying. International applicants should, however, separately consider any immigration, visa, travel or residency requirements that may apply if they are selected. Indigenous Applicants Are Particularly Encouraged The Shadbolt Fellowship has a specific commitment to decolonization and Indigenization. SFU states that the programme especially welcomes Indigenous applicants. The fellowship is not restricted to Indigenous applicants, but the university s commitment means that Indigenous scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers are particularly encouraged to submit applications. Applicants whose proposed projects engage meaningfully with Indigenous knowledge, decolonization, Indigenization or related areas may find strong alignment with the programme s stated mission. Commitment to Equity, Inclusion and Diversity The selection of resident Shadbolt Fellows will be guided by considerations of equity, inclusion and diversity. SFU also aims to ensure that its group of resident fellows represents a broad range of humanities and arts areas. The fellowship seeks to include: Indigenous applicants Emerging scholars and practitioners Established scholars and practitioners Academic scholars Artists Knowledge keepers Practitioners Writers Applicants working across different humanities and arts disciplines Candidates belonging to underrepresented groups are particularly encouraged to apply. These groups include: Indigenous peoples Persons with disabilities Racialized persons Women People representing gender and sexual diversity Applicants should nevertheless focus on presenting a strong project, relevant experience and a clear explanation of why SFU is an appropriate environment for their work. What Does the Fellowship Support? The Shadbolt Fellowship is designed to support projects that contribute to the humanities and arts as important spaces for creative practice and critical engagement with major concerns of our times. The programme aims to support work that can help society imagine better ways of understanding and shaping the world. Supported approaches may include: Creative arts Humanities research Publicly engaged scholarship Critical inquiry Cultural work Intellectual engagement Creative practice Socially engaged projects Decolonization Indigenization Interdisciplinary work Applicants should focus on the project they intend to undertake during the fellowship rather than simply describing their previous accomplishments. Their previous work should instead demonstrate their preparation and ability to successfully undertake the proposed project. Application Requirements Applicants must submit a complete application package containing the required documents. The application should include: 1. Completed Application Form Applicants must complete the official Shadbolt Fellowship Application Form for the 2027–28 academic year. The application form provides the required structure for the submission and should be completed accurately and thoroughly. 2. Current CV Applicants must provide a current curriculum vitae. The CV should clearly demonstrate the applicant s academic, artistic, professional, creative and/or public engagement background. Depending on the applicant s field, relevant information may include: Education Academic appointments Research experience Publications Books Articles Creative works Exhibitions Performances Professional experience Awards Fellowships Community engagement Public scholarship Artistic achievements Presentations Relevant projects Other professional or intellectual accomplishments 3. Cover Letter Applicants must also submit a cover letter. The cover letter should specifically address three areas identified by Simon Fraser University: The project the applicant intends to undertake during the fellowship. The desired primary unit affiliation in the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences and, where applicable, a secondary unit affiliation. The length of fellowship desired and why that duration is appropriate. Applicants should therefore avoid submitting a generic cover letter. The letter should be tailored specifically to the Shadbolt Fellowship and explain the applicant s proposed project, experience and connection to SFU. Choosing an SFU Primary Affiliation An important part of the application is identifying the academic unit where the applicant would like to be primarily affiliated. The primary affiliation should be within the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. Applicants should consider which department or programme best matches their proposed project and intellectual interests. A suitable affiliation can help demonstrate that the applicant has carefully considered how their work would fit within SFU s academic environment. Secondary Unit Affiliation Applicants may also identify a secondary affiliation if appropriate. Importantly, SFU states that secondary units may be any unit within Simon Fraser University and are not restricted to FASS. This creates an opportunity for applicants whose projects are interdisciplinary to identify another relevant academic unit that could contribute to their work. Applicants should only identify a secondary affiliation where it has a meaningful connection to the proposed project. Contacting an SFU Department Before Applying Before submitting an application, candidates are strongly encouraged to contact the FASS department or unit with which they wish to work. This is an important preparatory step. Applicants can use the opportunity to discuss: Their proposed project The relevance of the project to the department Potential academic connections Their proposed primary affiliation Possible secondary affiliations Interdisciplinary opportunities The fit between their project and SFU s academic environment Candidates can consult the official FASS departments and programmes list to identify the most appropriate unit. Fellowship Duration Applicants must indicate the length of fellowship they would like. They must also explain why the requested duration is appropriate. When determining the requested length, applicants should consider: The scope of their project Research requirements Creative development Writing requirements Public engagement activities Collaboration Access to university resources Expected project outcomes The amount of work that can realistically be completed The requested fellowship length should therefore be justified by the proposed project rather than selected without explanation. Application Deadline The application deadline for the 2027–28 Shadbolt Fellowship is: October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Applicants should ensure that their complete application package is submitted before the stated deadline. Applications should be emailed to: shadbolt_fellows@sfu.ca Simon Fraser University states that a single PDF is preferred. Applicants should also include their name in the filename. For example: FirstName_LastName_Shaddbolt_Fellowship_2027-28.pdf Applicants should follow the official application instructions when preparing and submitting their documents. Application Timeline The official timeline for the 2027–28 fellowship is as follows: September 21, 2026 — Online Q A Information Session An online question-and-answer information session will be held on September 21, 2026. Time: 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. Format: Online via Zoom This session provides prospective applicants with an opportunity to learn more about the fellowship and ask questions before submitting their applications. October 23, 2026 — Application Deadline The complete application must be submitted by: 9:00 a.m. on October 23, 2026. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final minutes to submit their applications. Late November — Shortlisted Candidates Notified Shortlisted candidates are expected to be notified in late November. December 7, 2026 — Reference Letters Deadline For shortlisted candidates, reference letters must be submitted by December 7, 2026. Applicants should therefore consider potential referees before the application deadline so they are prepared if shortlisted. Important Eligibility Restrictions Although the fellowship has broad eligibility in terms of professional background, SFU has identified important restrictions. Current SFU Students Individuals who are students at Simon Fraser University are ineligible for the fellowship. Continuing SFU Appointments Individuals who hold a continuing appointment at Simon Fraser University are also ineligible. Relationship to Degree Requirements SFU states that the project proposed for the fellowship will normally not be related to work being undertaken to fulfill the requirements of a degree programme in which the applicant is enrolled. The fellowship project should therefore generally be independent from an existing degree requirement. What Could Make an Application Strong? While applicants should follow the official requirements rather than trying to predict the selection committee, a strong application should be clear, focused and closely aligned with the goals of the fellowship. Present a Clearly Defined Project Explain exactly what you want to accomplish during the fellowship. The selection committee should be able to understand the project s purpose, objectives, intellectual direction or creative contribution. Demonstrate Humanities or Arts Relevance Clearly explain how the proposed work contributes to the humanities and/or arts. Explain the Broader Significance Where appropriate, demonstrate how the project engages with important cultural, social, intellectual or public issues. Show Why SFU Is a Good Fit Explain why Simon Fraser University is an appropriate environment for the proposed work. Identify the relevant primary unit and, where applicable, secondary affiliation. Demonstrate Feasibility The project should be realistic within the fellowship period requested. Applicants should demonstrate that they have thought carefully about what they can accomplish during their time as a fellow. Connect Your Experience to the Project Your CV and cover letter should establish a logical connection between your previous experience and the proposed fellowship project. Your past work should demonstrate that you have the skills, knowledge or creative experience necessary to undertake the project successfully. Recommended Preparation Checklist Applicants can prepare for the competition by following these steps: Read the official fellowship application form carefully. Develop a clear and meaningful fellowship project. Identify the most appropriate FASS department or unit. Consider whether a secondary SFU affiliation would strengthen the project. Contact the relevant department before submitting the application. Update your CV. Prepare a fellowship-specific cover letter. Clearly explain your desired fellowship duration. Review all eligibility restrictions. Complete the application form carefully. Combine the required documents into a single PDF where possible. Include your name in the PDF filename. Email the completed application to shadbolt_fellows@sfu.ca. Submit before October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. If shortlisted, ensure that reference letters are submitted by December 7, 2026. Frequently Asked Questions Is the Shadbolt Fellowship a scholarship? No. It is a fellowship supporting emerging and established scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers in the humanities and arts. Who is the fellowship designed for? The fellowship is designed for engaged academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers working in the humanities and arts. Can international applicants apply? The announcement does not specify a nationality restriction, so the opportunity is not limited to Canadian applicants. International candidates may apply provided they satisfy the stated eligibility requirements. Are Indigenous applicants encouraged to apply? Yes. SFU explicitly states that the programme especially welcomes Indigenous applicants and supports work connected to decolonization and Indigenization. Can current SFU students apply? No. Individuals who are students at SFU are ineligible. Can someone with a continuing SFU appointment apply? No. Individuals who hold a continuing appointment at SFU are ineligible. Do applicants have to be university professors? No. The fellowship specifically includes artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers in addition to academic scholars. Does the primary affiliation have to be within FASS? Yes. Applicants are asked to identify their desired primary unit affiliation within the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. Can the secondary affiliation be outside FASS? Yes. SFU states that secondary units may be any unit within Simon Fraser University. Should applicants contact a department before applying? Yes. SFU strongly encourages candidates to contact the FASS department or unit with which they wish to work before submitting their applications. What documents are required? Applicants must submit: A fully completed application form A current CV A cover letter A single PDF is preferred. What is the application deadline? The application deadline is October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. When will shortlisted candidates be notified? Shortlisted candidates are expected to be notified in late November. When are reference letters due? Reference letters for shortlisted candidates are due December 7, 2026. Official Application Information Prospective applicants should carefully review the official Simon Fraser University fellowship information and application materials before submitting their applications. Official application page Official 2027–28 application form More fellowship available on the OFY Website HERE Conclusion The Jack and Doris Shadbolt Fellowship in the Humanities 2027–28 at Simon Fraser University provides an important opportunity for emerging and established academic scholars, artists, knowledge keepers, practitioners and writers to develop meaningful work within a university environment dedicated to the humanities and arts. The fellowship stands out because of its broad understanding of who can contribute to the humanities and arts. Applicants do not have to fit exclusively within the traditional academic model, as the programme welcomes artists, writers, practitioners and knowledge keepers alongside academic scholars. The programme also places strong emphasis on creative practice, publicly engaged scholarship, critical engagement with major concerns of our time, decolonization and Indigenization. Indigenous applicants are particularly encouraged to apply, while candidates from underrepresented groups are also strongly encouraged to consider the opportunity. Applicants should prepare a complete application consisting of the official application form, a current CV and a tailored cover letter. The cover letter should explain the proposed fellowship project, desired primary and secondary affiliations and the requested fellowship duration. Candidates are also strongly encouraged to contact their preferred FASS department or unit before submitting their application. The key deadline to remember is October 23, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Shortlisted candidates are expected to be notified in late November, while reference letters for shortlisted candidates will be due on December 7, 2026. For individuals whose work combines humanities, arts, culture, scholarship, creativity or public engagement, the Shadbolt Fellowship could provide a valuable platform to develop an ambitious project, engage with an academic community and contribute to broader intellectual, cultural and social conversations. For the upcoming 2027 Winter/Spring Session , applications are open from August 24 to September 11, 2026 , while the internship itself will run from January 14, 2027, to April 30, 2027 .
